clue.text: No longer having old chair that's worth being kept by girl in recession

indicators.note: something kept by another is held within it, so one piece sits inside the other
a recession is a going back, so the girl's name is read backwards

parts.note: Sue is a girl's name
worth means merit

explanation.surface: A professor who has lost their old chair is valued and looked after by a young woman during an economic downturn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in recession' reads like economics but turns the girl's name to EUS; an emeritus professor has given up the chair.
explanation.definitionFit: An emeritus professor has retired from the post but keeps the title as an honour.

clue.text: Unfinished creamy dish, also known as a Greek speciality

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: mousse is a light creamy dish

explanation.surface: An incomplete creamy pudding, otherwise called a Greek delicacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfinished' drops the final E from MOUSSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Moussaka is a baked dish of aubergine and minced meat, a classic of Greek cooking.

clue.text: Very English, say? Then land in New England

parts.note: real is used informally to mean very
to say is to state

explanation.surface: A question about being terribly English, then landing in a region of the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in New England' marks the definition as American usage for landed property.
explanation.definitionFit: Real estate is the American term for property in land and buildings.

clue.text: Repetition of letters as infant training?

definitions.text: Repetition of letters as infant training?

parts.words: Repetition of letters as infant training?
parts.note: one letter repeated three times, which is also the name for basic schooling in reading, writing and arithmetic

explanation.surface: Children are trained by repeating the alphabet.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are reading, (w)riting and (a)rithmetic, the basics of early schooling; the clue plays on R appearing three times.
explanation.definitionFit: Elementary education is summed up as reading, writing and arithmetic.

clue.text: Opponents at table battle openly, without protection of this

parts.note: in bridge, South and East are opponents at the table
Crecy was a 1346 battle between England and France

explanation.surface: Rivals at a card table fight in the open without cover.
explanation.walkthrough: Doing something openly is doing it without the cover of concealment.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting openly means acting without the protection of concealment.

clue.text: Entrance examination shunned by university

indicators.note: shunned by means left out, so the university letter goes

parts.note: an audit is an examination of accounts

explanation.surface: University students avoid an entrance exam.
explanation.walkthrough: An adit is a horizontal entrance to a mine.
explanation.definitionFit: An adit is a horizontal passage into a mine, so an entrance.

clue.text: Apply antiseptic to sheep, to improve appearance

parts.note: tar was applied to sheep's sores as an antiseptic
a tup is a ram

explanation.surface: A farmer dabs disinfectant on a ram to make it look better.
explanation.definitionFit: To tart up something is to smarten or decorate it, often cheaply.

clue.text: Animal died without clothes being worn

indicators.note: without means outside, so the animal goes around the clothes

parts.note: a doe is a female deer
gear is clothing

explanation.surface: A creature dies with no clothes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as lacking, but means outside: DO(GEAR)E, then D.
explanation.definitionFit: Dog-eared pages are worn and shabby from use.

clue.text: Essentially help artist to gatecrash parties in rich land, so many thought

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so the middle letters of help are taken
a gatecrasher pushes into a party, so the artist goes inside the parties

parts.note: two parties, each a do
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: Someone advises an artist to crash parties in a wealthy place that people once believed in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parties' gives two DOs, which the artist splits; 'Essentially' takes the core of help. 'so many thought' marks El Dorado as legendary.
explanation.definitionFit: El Dorado was the legendary city of gold, a land of riches that explorers believed existed.

clue.text: Crescent-shaped inlay regularly set into musical instrument

indicators.note: set into means placed inside, so the picked letters go within the instrument

parts.note: a lute is a stringed musical instrument

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of inlay

explanation.surface: A crescent-shaped inlay is routinely fitted into a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of inlay, which are then 'set into' the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunate comes from the Latin for moon and describes a crescent outline.

clue.text: Go over performance by sort of dove

parts.note: a turn is a performance or act on a variety bill
the turtle, or turtle dove, is a kind of dove

explanation.surface: Someone reviews a show put on by a type of pigeon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go over' reads like revising, but it means capsize.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn turtle is to capsize, as a boat that flips over with its keel uppermost.

clue.text: Cuckoo's nest, abandoned, not completely round

definitions.note: read as 'Cuckoo is', with the definition an adjective meaning crazy

indicators.note: turned round means read in the other direction
only part of the words nest abandoned is used, the run straddling them

explanation.surface: A cuckoo has left its nest, which is not quite round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not completely' picks STAB out of neST ABandoned, and 'round' turns it to BATS.
explanation.definitionFit: Bats is informal for crazy, as in having bats in the belfry.

clue.text: One related to King cooked pork chop given to Queen

indicators.note: cooked means doctored or messed about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A relative of the monarch has cooked a pork chop for the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges PORKCHOP into ROCKHOPP. King here is the king penguin, not a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The rockhopper is a small crested penguin, a relative of the king penguin.

clue.text: Typically, lead guitar is thrashed in it

definitions.meaning: lead is a typical example of a dense poisonous element of that class
loud rock music in which electric guitars are played hard

explanation.surface: Usually the lead guitarist plays fiercely in this music.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a class of dense elements like lead and a loud rock genre.

clue.text: His argument's well known to be three-sided

definitions.text: His argument's well known to be three-sided

parts.words: His argument's well known to be three-sided
parts.note: the Greek mathematician whose famous theorem concerns right-angled triangles

explanation.surface: A man whose famous case has three sides to it.
explanation.definitionFit: His theorem relates the sides of a right-angled triangle, the best-known proof in geometry.

clue.text: Rabbit made of china by state

parts.note: china is Cockney rhyming slang for mate (china plate), so a pal
to state is to aver, to declare

explanation.surface: A porcelain rabbit is produced by a state.
explanation.walkthrough: Rabbit here is the verb from rhyming slang (rabbit and pork, talk); china plate means mate. Both are Cockney rhyming slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabbit is British slang for chatter, and palaver is lengthy, idle talk or fuss.

clue.text: It has letters on numbers and letters on letters

definitions.text: It has letters on numbers and letters on letters

parts.words: It has letters on numbers and letters on letters
parts.note: a mixed code of letters and digits written on mail

explanation.surface: A riddle about something with letters and numbers on letters.
explanation.walkthrough: A UK address code like SW1A 1AA mixes letters and numbers and goes on envelopes.
explanation.definitionFit: A British mail code is made of letters and numbers and written on letters.

clue.text: In which one would wear out a whistle

definitions.text: In which one would wear out a whistle

parts.words: In which one would wear out a whistle
parts.note: whistle and flute is Cockney rhyming slang for suit, so this is the London district where you'd put on a whistle to go out

explanation.surface: A place where you might blow a whistle until it breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wear out' looks like using something up, but means wear when going out; whistle is a suit in rhyming slang, which belongs to the traditional Cockney district of east London.
explanation.definitionFit: The East End of London is the home of Cockney rhyming slang, where whistle means suit.

clue.text: Pay particular attention to fully developed new born

definitions.meaning: the Latin phrase means note well
the abbreviation NB, as for new born, written out in full

explanation.surface: Note especially a baby born at full term.
explanation.walkthrough: NB stands for new born, but it is also the abbreviation of this Latin phrase, so 'fully developed' means expanded.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means note well, telling the reader to take careful notice.

clue.text: Some people's ideal garden, that should secure a star?

definitions.text: Some people's ideal garden, that should secure a star?

parts.words: Some people's ideal garden, that should secure a star?
parts.note: a sheltered sunny spot, read as a snare that catches our star

explanation.surface: A garden good enough to earn a star rating.
explanation.walkthrough: The star is the sun, and secure means catch.
explanation.definitionFit: A suntrap is a sheltered place that gets a lot of sunshine.

clue.text: Place little animals by sink

parts.note: shrews are small mouse-like mammals
to sink something, as in the ground, is to bury it

explanation.surface: Someone puts small creatures next to a kitchen sink.
explanation.walkthrough: SHREWSBURY is the county town of Shropshire in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewsbury is a town in England, so a place.

clue.text: Comet was supposed to hit earth here!

definitions.text: Comet was supposed to hit earth here!

parts.words: Comet was supposed to hit earth here!
parts.note: Comet was a jet airliner, which was meant to touch down on a landing strip

explanation.surface: A warning about where a comet is due to strike.
explanation.walkthrough: The de Havilland Comet was the first jet airliner.
explanation.definitionFit: An airliner is meant to touch ground on the airport strip.

clue.text: Requested wife and daughter to split stake

indicators.note: to split is to leave, so these letters depart from the word

parts.note: requested means wanted
W is short for wife and D for daughter

explanation.surface: Someone asked for the wife and daughter to share a stake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'split' looks like dividing the stake, but means departing: W and D leave WANTED.
explanation.definitionFit: An ante is the stake a poker player puts in before the deal.

clue.text: Measure bird in the middle

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: the middle is the centre
bird is British slang for a prison sentence, time

explanation.surface: A gauge is used on a bird at its midpoint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' is not a creature here: doing bird is British slang for serving time in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A centimetre is a unit of length, so a measure.

clue.text: Catty remark from women, upset no end

indicators.note: upset means overturned or disturbed, so the letters are rearranged
no end means the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A spiteful comment from women who are upset without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end' leaves WOME, which 'upset' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat's cry is a fitting remark from a cat, so catty in a literal sense.

clue.text: Heartless guard's sometimes cold

indicators.note: heartless means without the central letter

parts.note: a turnkey is a jailer, a prison guard

explanation.surface: A guard without compassion is now and then chilly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' removes N, the middle letter of TURNKEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Cold turkey is abrupt withdrawal from a drug, so the word is sometimes preceded by cold.

clue.text: People moved out of area after military activities in attack approached from East

indicators.note: after puts the area's letter at the end
an across answer read from the east runs right to left, so it is backwards
in places the operations inside the attack

parts.note: a raid is an attack
ops are military operations

explanation.surface: Displaced people left a region after an army campaign during an assault from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' gives R(OPS)AID, which 'approached from East' turns to DIASPOR; 'after' puts A at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A diaspora is a people dispersed from their homeland.

clue.text: One European runs after another one that may be French

indicators.note: after puts the runs letter behind the other European

parts.note: Polish is one European language or nationality
another European, E being its abbreviation
R stands for runs in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: A European runs after another European.
explanation.walkthrough: A French polisher finishes wood with shellac, so 'French' is not about a nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: A French polisher is a craftsman who applies a high gloss shellac finish to wood.
